the_signal.headline: Multi-agent systems hit production—coordination failures are the new blocker
the_signal.body: Anthropic's research on multi-agent patterns and problems signals that the industry has moved past single-agent reliability into a harder problem: how agents coordinate, fail together, and create cascading errors. For GTM engineers building revenue systems, this means your automation framework needs explicit failure isolation and agent handoff validation—or you're shipping a system that breaks in unpredictable ways at scale.

tool_drop.name: jitpass (Show HN)
tool_drop.what: Secrets management that keeps plaintext credentials off your laptop—enforces encrypted storage at rest.
tool_drop.why: If you're shipping AI agents to production, leaked API keys to LLM providers tank your cost model and expose customer data; this moves credential handling from 'best practice' to 'non-negotiable ops requirement.'

thread_of_day.title: RPA vs. Workflow Automation: Building Automation That Lasts
thread_of_day.takeaway: RPA breaks on UI changes and doesn't scale; workflow automation (event-driven, API-first) is what production GTM systems actually need—reliability, security, and observability come from the architecture choice, not the tool.

quote.text: We don't know how much a token really costs. They are subsidized by big tech and most AI providers are operating at a loss.
quote.source: n8n Blog — Token prices won't increase if you host your own LLMs

whats_moving.context: Token subsidies are temporary; GTM teams betting margin on API pricing will face margin compression when providers normalize pricing to actual cost.
n8n's deep dive on auth methods signals operators are tightening security posture—expect customers to demand proof of secrets rotation and zero-plaintext policies.
Async APIs and event streams are becoming table stakes for multi-agent coordination; teams still using request-response loops will hit latency and failure mode walls.

act_on_this: Pull your agent failure logs from the last 30 days and map which failures come from agent-to-agent handoffs vs. single-agent issues; if >20% are coordination failures, you need explicit retry logic and dead-letter queues before shipping to production.
